comparison: Both evaluations support the PhyB-PIF optogenetic system's functionality (C33-C36, C95-C97). OpenEval emphasizes the system's characteristics (rapid, reversible, repeatable) with supporting data from Figure 1 supplement 1. Peer reviewers praised the system as 'innovative and well-executed' with comprehensive explanation in Figures 1 and 2. Peer review also covers C37-C38 (temporal dynamics), which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 addresses temporal dynamics and reversibility (C37-C38) supported by Figure 1 supplement 2. Peer R1 includes these claims as part of their broader evaluation of the optogenetic system, finding it comprehensively explained without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on the central finding that PI3K activation is sufficient for TRPV1 trafficking to plasma membrane (C39-C41). Both evaluations strongly support this claim. OpenEval notes the logical soundness of the inference based on pathway isolation. Peer reviewers unanimously endorsed this finding, with all three reviewers explicitly praising it, and noted that revised manuscript with new controls (Figure 4E) further strengthened the conclusion.

Complete agreement on reciprocal interaction between TRPV1 and PI3K (C42-C48). Both evaluations support the specificity controls with TRPM4 and PIF-YFP lacking iSH2. OpenEval notes the mechanistic speculation (C48) is appropriately labeled and based on prior work. Peer reviewers accepted this as evidence of 'reciprocal influence between an enzyme and a channel' without questioning the controls.

Both evaluations support successful ncAA incorporation without disrupting protein function (C49-C53). OpenEval cites functional assays in Figure 3 supplements 1-2. Peer reviewers strongly endorsed this methodological innovation, with Reviewer 2 calling it 'a great tool for those studying membrane proteins.' Peer R4 also covers dye selection (C54-C59) and kinetics (C60-C62), which OpenEval addresses separately.

OpenEval R6 addresses selective surface labeling with sTCO-sulfo-Cy5 (C54-C59), supported by systematic dye testing in Figure 3 supplement 3. Peer R4 includes these claims as part of their broader endorsement of the click chemistry methodology, praising the 'membrane-impermeable fluorescent probe' without questioning the dye selection rationale.

OpenEval R7 addresses kinetic measurements (C60-C62) supported by Figure 3D-F with appropriate literature comparisons. Peer R4 includes these claims in their overall methodological evaluation. Peer Reviewer 2 noted 'reaction rates were slow as noted by the authors' but still praised the technique's utility, accepting the kinetic characterization.

Perfect agreement on NGF-induced surface trafficking measured by click chemistry (C63-C67). Both evaluations support the findings and comparison to TIRF data. OpenEval notes vehicle controls confirm specificity. Peer reviewers particularly appreciated the quantitative analyses and new control experiments (Figure 4E) added in revision, with Reviewer 3 finding them 'convincingly demonstrate specificity.'

Complete agreement on light-induced surface trafficking for both TRPV1 and InsR (C68-C72). Both evaluations support the findings demonstrating PI3K sufficiency. OpenEval notes TRPV1-specific 750 nm effect and control experiments. Peer reviewers praised the control experiments (Figure 5 supplement 1) as convincingly demonstrating specificity of stimuli.

Perfect agreement on the novel finding of PI3K regulation of insulin receptor trafficking (C73, C92). Both evaluations accept this as valid new observation. OpenEval notes the physiological significance requires further investigation. Peer reviewers accepted the finding's validity, though one noted InsR findings felt 'somewhat tangential' to the main story, but did not question the result itself.

OpenEval R11 addresses functional validation of labeled TRPV1 (C78) and empirical knowledge about ncAA incorporation (C79). Peer R8 includes C78-C79 as part of broader methodological assessment, accepting these claims without challenge as part of the technique's validation.

Both evaluations support the assessment of current limitations and future directions (C80-C83). OpenEval notes these represent honest assessment of technical limitations. Peer reviewers accepted these methodological assessments, with Reviewer 2 noting slow reaction rates but still praising utility. Both appreciate transparency about constraints.

OpenEval R13 addresses advantages of ncAA approach (C76-C77) as reasonable inferences about minimal perturbation. Peer R8 includes these claims in their broader methodological evaluation, accepting the advantages without challenge and appreciating the discussion of benefits and limitations.

Perfect agreement on technical limitations for in vivo applications (C84-C86). Both evaluations accept these as accurate descriptions of current constraints. OpenEval notes honest assessment of technology's limitations. Peer reviewers acknowledged limitations without dispute, though Reviewer 2 suggested limitations discussion may have been overemphasized relative to biological significance.

OpenEval R15 addresses extensive background claims (C1-C32, C87-C94) establishing context and identifying knowledge gaps, all appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings and methodological innovations rather than evaluating background literature claims.
